CLOCK_MODE().details: Machine-readable description of the clock as specified in ERC-6372.

actualizarGuardian(address).details: [CORRECCIÓN DOCENTE - PUNTO 5] Garantiza que el rol de Guardián esté subordinado a la asamblea.

params.nuevoGuardian: Nueva dirección autorizada para cancelar propuestas en cola durante emergencias.

cancelarPropuestaEnCola(address[],uint25.details: [CORRECCIÓN DOCENTE - PUNTO 5] Materializa la ventana de seguridad del Timelock: si tras aprobarse      una propuesta se detecta un error en el presupuesto, un problema con el contratista o una emergencia      edilicia antes de que venza el `minDelay`, el `guardian` (Síndico) o el `proposalProposer` original      pueden cancelar la operación encolada. Internamente invoca `_cancel(...)`, que marca la propuesta como      `Canceled` en `ConsorcioGovernor` y ejecuta `_timelock.cancel(timelockId)` usando el `CANCELLER_ROLE`.

params.calldatas: Lista de payloads codificados de la propuesta encolada.
params.descriptionHash: Hash `keccak256` de la descripción original de la propuesta.
params.targets: Lista de contratos destino de la propuesta encolada.
params.values: Lista de montos en wei de la propuesta encolada.

clock().details: Clock (as specified in ERC-6372) is set to match the token's clock. Fallback to block numbers if the token does not implement ERC-6372.

params._proposalThreshold: Mínimo de unidades requeridas para crear una propuesta (ej. 0 o 1 unidad).
params._quorumPercentage: Porcentaje de quórum requerido sobre el total de unidades (`30 <= q <= 100`).
params._timelock: Contrato `ConsorcioTimelock` que custodia y ejecuta las órdenes sobre `ConsorcioObras`.
params._token: Contrato `ConsorcioVotes` (implementa `IVotes` con reloj en modo timestamp).
params._votingDelay: Período de deliberación antes de abrir la votación (ej. 86400 = 1 día).
params._votingPeriod: Duración de la ventana de votación (ej. 432000 = 5 días; debe ser > 0).

hashProposal(address[],uint256[],bytes[].details: See {IGovernor-hashProposal}. The proposal id is produced by hashing the ABI encoded `targets` array, the `values` array, the `calldatas` array and the descriptionHash (bytes32 which itself is the keccak256 hash of the description string). This proposal id can be produced from the proposal data which is part of the {ProposalCreated} event. It can even be computed in advance, before the proposal is submitted. Note that the chainId and the governor address are not part of the proposal id computation. Consequently, the same proposal (with same operation and same description) will have the same id if submitted on multiple governors across multiple networks. This also means that in order to execute the same operation twice (on the same governor) the proposer will have to change the description in order to avoid proposal id conflicts.

nonces(address).details: Returns the next unused nonce for an address.

onERC1155BatchReceived(address,address,u.details: See {IERC1155Receiver-onERC1155BatchReceived}. Receiving tokens is disabled if the governance executor is other than the governor itself (eg. when using with a timelock).

onERC1155Received(address,address,uint25.details: See {IERC1155Receiver-onERC1155Received}. Receiving tokens is disabled if the governance executor is other than the governor itself (eg. when using with a timelock).

onERC721Received(address,address,uint256.details: See {IERC721Receiver-onERC721Received}. Receiving tokens is disabled if the governance executor is other than the governor itself (eg. when using with a timelock).

proposalNeedsQueuing(uint256).details: Whether a proposal needs to be queued before execution.

proposalVotes(uint256).details: Accessor to the internal vote counts.

propose(address[],uint256[],bytes[],stri.details: See {IGovernor-propose}. This function has opt-in frontrunning protection, described in {_isValidDescriptionForProposer}.

quorum(uint256).details: Minimum number of cast voted required for a proposal to be successful. NOTE: The `timepoint` parameter corresponds to the snapshot used for counting vote. This allows to scale the quorum depending on values such as the totalSupply of a token at this timepoint (see {ERC20Votes}).

quorumDenominator().details: Returns the quorum denominator. Defaults to 100, but may be overridden.

quorumNumerator().details: Returns the current quorum numerator. See {quorumDenominator}.

quorumNumerator(uint256).details: Returns the quorum numerator at a specific timepoint. See {quorumDenominator}.

relay(address,uint256,bytes).details: Relays a transaction or function call to an arbitrary target. In cases where the governance executor is some contract other than the governor itself, like when using a timelock, this function can be invoked in a governance proposal to recover tokens or Ether that was sent to the governor contract by mistake. Note that if the executor is simply the governor itself, use of `relay` is redundant.

setProposalThreshold(uint256).details: Update the proposal threshold. This operation can only be performed through a governance proposal. Emits a {ProposalThresholdSet} event.

setVotingDelay(uint48).details: Update the voting delay. This operation can only be performed through a governance proposal. Emits a {VotingDelaySet} event.

setVotingPeriod(uint32).details: Update the voting period. This operation can only be performed through a governance proposal. Emits a {VotingPeriodSet} event.

state(uint256).details: Current state of a proposal, following Compound's convention

timelock().details: Public accessor to check the address of the timelock

token().details: The token that voting power is sourced from.

updateQuorumNumerator(uint256).details: Changes the quorum numerator. Emits a {QuorumNumeratorUpdated} event. Requirements: - Must be called through a governance proposal. - New numerator must be smaller or equal to the denominator.

updateTimelock(address).details: Public endpoint to update the underlying timelock instance. Restricted to the timelock itself, so updates must be proposed, scheduled, and executed through governance proposals. CAUTION: It is not recommended to change the timelock while there are other queued governance proposals.

votingDelay().details: Delay, between the proposal is created and the vote starts. The unit this duration is expressed in depends on the clock (see ERC-6372) this contract uses. This can be increased to leave time for users to buy voting power, or delegate it, before the voting of a proposal starts. NOTE: While this interface returns a uint256, timepoints are stored as uint48 following the ERC-6372 clock type. Consequently this value must fit in a uint48 (when added to the current clock). See {IERC6372-clock}.

votingPeriod().details: Delay between the vote start and vote end. The unit this duration is expressed in depends on the clock (see ERC-6372) this contract uses. NOTE: The {votingDelay} can delay the start of the vote. This must be considered when setting the voting duration compared to the voting delay. NOTE: This value is stored when the proposal is submitted so that possible changes to the value do not affect proposals that have already been submitted. The type used to save it is a uint32. Consequently, while this interface returns a uint256, the value it returns should fit in a uint32.

@title ConsorcioGovernor
 @author Equipo ConsorcioDAO - ETH Kipu Nivel 2
 @notice Contrato de Gobernanza de la comunidad (Consorcio de edificio o Country).
 @dev Generado y estructurado siguiendo el estándar de OpenZeppelin Contracts Wizard v5:
      https://wizard.openzeppelin.com/#governor
      y las plantillas de referencia:
      - https://github.com/PatrickAlphaC/dao-template
      - https://github.com/Cyfrin/foundry-dao-cu
      Módulos integrados:
      - `GovernorSettings`: Configura período de deliberación previo (`votingDelay`),
        duración de la votación (`votingPeriod`) y umbral mínimo para proponer (`proposalThreshold`).
      - `GovernorCountingSimple`: Votación estándar (0 = En Contra, 1 = A Favor, 2 = Abstención).
      - `GovernorVotes`: Extrae el peso de voto desde `ConsorcioVotes` (`ERC721Votes`) según el snapshot histórico.
      - `GovernorVotesQuorumFraction`: Define el quórum como porcentaje de unidades totales (`30%` a `100%`).
      - `GovernorTimelockControl`: Encola y ejecuta todas las decisiones aprobadas a través de `ConsorcioTimelock`.
      =========================================================================
      CORRECCIONES DE MENTORÍA DOCENTE IMPLEMENTADAS EN ESTE CONTRATO:
      =========================================================================
      1. [CORRECCIÓN DOCENTE - PUNTO 1] (Quórum estatutario mínimo del 30% al 50%):
         - Observación: Con `GovernorVotesQuorumFraction` al 4% y pocas unidades funcionales (`< 25`),
           la división entera `(totalSupply * 4) / 100` trunca a `0`, permitiendo aprobar propuestas con 1 solo voto.
         - Solución implementada: Se eleva `QUORUM_MINIMO` a `30` (30%) y se despliega el consorcio con un
           quórum estatutario del `50%` (rango recomendado 30%–50% acorde al régimen de asambleas del CCyC).
           Con `quorumDenominator() == 100` constante en OpenZeppelin, jamás existe división por cero, y para
           todo consorcio constituido (`totalSupply >= 4` unidades) el quórum exige al menos 2 unidades
           (`(4 * 50) / 100 = 2`), verificado formalmente con pruebas de invariantes en Foundry y Echidna.
         - Nota de arquitectura (Alternativa teórica no requerida en código): Otra variante posible en sistemas
           con `quorumNumerator` muy bajo (<10%) consiste en sobreescribir `quorum(uint256 timepoint)` aplicando
           redondeo hacia arriba `(supply * num + 99) / 100` o un piso fijo `max(super.quorum(t), MIN_VOTES)`.
           Al fijar `QUORUM_MINIMO = 30` y operar al `50%`, el cálculo nativo de OpenZeppelin resuelve el problema
           sin alterar la fórmula estándar auditada.
      2. [CORRECCIÓN DOCENTE - PUNTO 5] (Cancelación de propuestas en estado `Queued` durante `minDelay`):
         - Observación: `ConsorcioGovernor` recibe `CANCELLER_ROLE` en `ConsorcioTimelock`, pero en OpenZeppelin v5
           la función pública `cancel()` solo permite al proponente cancelar mientras la propuesta está en `Pending`.
           Una vez aprobada y encolada (`Queued`), no existía una función expuesta para cancelarla durante la
           ventana de seguridad (`minDelay`) del Timelock.
         - Solución implementada: Se incorpora el rol `guardian` (Síndico / Auditor de seguridad, actualizable
           por gobernanza) y la función externa `cancelarPropuestaEnCola(...)`, que permite al `guardian` o al
           proponente original cancelar una propuesta en estado `Queued` invocando `_cancel(...)`, lo cual revoca
           la operación tanto en el Governor como en `ConsorcioTimelock` antes de que venza el `minDelay`.
